## Summary

Preserve the resolved Request headers when forwarding fetchOptions. On Node 24, a previously polluted Object.prototype.headers can otherwise replace caller headers during the native RequestInit conversion. This does not introduce a prototype-pollution primitive; it fixes the publicly reported read-side behavior.

## Linked issue

Fixes #11263.

## Changes

- Forward the resolved Request's headers as an own fetch option, including headers generated by Request for its body.
- Add six loopback regressions covering empty, cache and redirect options with and without an inherited Authorization canary.
- Keep custom fetch options and frozen caller options intact. Update the existing custom-fetch expectation and add the required prerelease note.

#### Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated
- [x] Docs/types updated if public API changed: no public API or declaration change; prerelease note added
- [x] No breaking changes: custom fetch receives headers matching the resolved Request

Verification: exact-base regressions fail in three polluted cases and pass in three clean controls. The executed isolated verify.sh passes the patched public reproduction, all 1,296 unit tests, repository ESLint and the declaration type check. All 23 browser test files pass separately in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: 265 passed and one existing skipped test per browser. (These results come from the package builder; I did not rerun them.)

Caveats: the initial combined browser runs hit session startup timeouts; isolated unchanged suites passed. Node 22, Bun, Deno and packed CJS/module smoke suites were not executed. PR #11177 addresses a different inherited Symbol.iterator path and still forwards headerless fetch options; a rebase may be needed if it lands first. Maintainers may prefer a different security-fix approach.

Instinct assisted. :surfer:

## Description
